_README: Copy this file to seed_identity.json and replace every value with your own.
The core idea: you are the source, resumes are compiled output.
evidence         = things that actually exist and can be checked (a paper, a repo, a project, a URL).
capability_units = what you can do, each one POINTING AT the evidence that proves it.
Nothing is ever claimed on a resume unless it traces back to an evidence entry.
That is what stops the system inventing things about you.
Start small. Six evidence entries and four capability units is enough to produce
a first application package. Add more as you go.

profile.name: Your Name
profile.title: The one-line positioning you want at the top of a resume
profile.work_rights: State your status plainly — 'Australian citizen', 'Permanent resident', or your visa subclass and its expiry. The reviewer checks this against each ad and flags roles that conflict with it. If you are a citizen or PR, also empty VISA_BLOCKERS in proteus/fit.py.
profile.summary: Three or four sentences you would be happy to read aloud in an interview. Plain words, no adjectives you cannot defend.

bullets: What you actually did, with real numbers. Scale beats adjectives.
One line per distinct thing. Keep the strongest first.

personas.builder: Software and data positioning: pipelines, tooling, shipped systems.
personas.manager: Coordination positioning: budgets, reporting, multi-party delivery.
personas.polymath: Mixed positioning — used when a job spans more than one of the above.

evidence.ref: Full citation, with a DOI or URL if there is one.
evidence.note: Anything that makes it stronger — a prize, an invitation, a citation count.

evidence.ref: Project name, your role, scale in real numbers (budget, people, sites, duration).
evidence.note: Say plainly whether you led it or contributed to it. Do not inflate this.

evidence.ref: What you built, the stack, and where the code lives.

capability_units.statement: One sentence on what you can do. Be specific about the limit too — 'independently does X; has not yet done Y' is more credible than a bare claim, and keeps you honest in interviews.
keywords: the words a job ad would actually use for this

capability_units.statement: A second capability, pointing at different evidence.
